caption:
Part 2. One of you said GO. 🦊🏮
So you followed the fox into the old forest, with footsteps behind you matching yours.

Hundreds of lanterns. Your neighbors underneath, eyes shut, smiling. And one lantern with your name on it.

At sunrise you all walked home. Except the fox. Its lantern is fading, and sunset is at 5:41.
Go back for the fox, or stay home? Your call: comment GO or STAY 👇 The majority writes Part 3.

part3.title: Lantern Night · Part 3
part3.ending: Part 3 closes the series. The thing in the dark only finds eyes that are open and looking; one night a year the fox, keeper of the lanterns, keeps the whole town hidden, and it can never shut its own eyes, because someone has to hold the light. GO: at dusk you walk back in with no lantern, eyes shut, following its fading glow; you take the stick from the fox and hold the light yourself until dawn, so for the first time the fox can close its eyes and sleep; the footsteps pass you by; at sunrise you both walk home, and the fox's lantern now hangs at your window: next Lantern Night, you hold it together. STAY: you stay home, but at 2:07 am you light the lantern with your name and put it in your window; the fox's light goes out in the forest, then a small glow comes across the field towards yours, and the fox climbs onto your windowsill, safe; the footsteps stop at your door and turn away. Both endings end warm, with a last question to comment (not a new choice).
